prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of proposals (within 500 words)

Economy and jobs
- Invest in renewables and a national home‑energy upgrade to cut bills and create jobs; publish a long‑term industrial strategy focused on green, digital and life‑science sectors.
- Expand apprenticeships and introduce Lifelong Skills Grants; replace the apprenticeship levy with a flexible skills levy.
- Support small businesses with a reformed business rates system (moving to a Commercial Landowner Levy), stronger British Business Bank, late‑payment enforcement and local banking.
- Make taxation fairer by reversing recent bank tax cuts, increasing the Digital Services Tax, reforming capital gains, and adding a 4% levy on large share buybacks.
- Modernise worker protections: a new “dependent contractor” status, stronger sick pay, rights for zero‑hours workers, a living‑wage review, and a single Worker Protection Enforcement Authority.
- Regulate AI with clear, innovation‑friendly rules and transparency for public‑sector use.

Climate, energy and nature
- Reach net zero by 2045; 90% of electricity from renewables by 2030; zero‑carbon standards for all new homes.
- Free insulation and heat pumps for low‑income households; rooftop solar incentives; social energy tariff; decouple electricity prices from gas; expand storage and interconnectors; support community energy.
- Maintain bans on fracking and new coal; end fossil‑fuel subsidies with a just transition.
- End sewage discharges with tougher regulation, company reform and a sewage tax; binding targets to restore biodiversity; plant 60m trees a year; new Clean Air Act and Air Quality Agency; deposit return scheme and rapid cut in non‑recyclable single‑use plastics; major peatland and blue‑carbon restoration; protect 30% of land and sea by 2030.

Health and social care
- Legal right to see a GP within seven days (24 hours if urgent) via 8,000 more GPs and greater roles for pharmacists; guarantee urgent NHS dentistry; community mental‑health hubs and a professional in every school; cancer treatment within 62 days.
- Invest in staff retention, pay review independence, ambulance and hospital capacity, interoperable IT, virtual wards and diagnostics.
- Reform drugs policy with more treatment and a regulated cannabis market for adults.
- Introduce free personal care, a national care workforce plan, a Royal College of Care Workers, a higher Carer’s Minimum Wage, paid carers’ leave, regular respite, and stronger support for kinship care.

Education and families
- Raise per‑pupil funding above inflation and fix buildings; tutoring for disadvantaged pupils; stronger SEND funding and a national body; teacher workforce plan and CPD; lifelong learning grants; restore maintenance grants.
- Expand early‑years support and extend free school meals to children in poverty.
- Overhaul parental leave and pay (day‑one rights, higher statutory rates, extra use‑it‑or‑lose‑it month for partners); review childcare funding; rejoin Erasmus+ for young people.

Housing and communities
- Build 380,000 homes a year, including 150,000 social homes; new garden cities; enable councils to buy land at existing‑use value; prioritise brownfield; “use‑it‑or‑lose‑it” permissions; remove unsafe cladding at no leaseholder cost; abolish leasehold and cap ground rents.
- Ban no‑fault evictions, make three‑year tenancies the default, create a landlord register; allow local ending of Right to Buy; introduce rent‑to‑own; plan to end rough sleeping; give councils powers over second homes and short‑term lets.
- Multi‑year council funding and nationwide gigabit broadband.

Transport
- Accelerate EV rollout (more chargers, 5% VAT on public charging, restore plug‑in grant, 2030 zero‑emission sales mandate).
- Freeze rail fares, simplify ticketing, establish a new Railway Agency, deliver Northern Powerhouse Rail, expand electrification; empower bus franchising and create a single local bus fund; national active‑travel strategy.
- Shift freight to rail; reform flight taxes to target frequent flyers and private jets; restrict short domestic flights where fast rail exists; moratorium on net airport expansion.

Crime and justice
- Restore community policing; guarantee attendance for burglaries; clear court backlogs; create an Online Crime Agency; replace elected commissioners with local policing boards; expand youth diversion; strengthen modern‑slavery enforcement; improve prisons, rehabilitation and resettlement; enhance international cooperation.

Immigration and asylum
- Move work/student visa policy to relevant departments; adopt flexible, sector‑based visas; reverse recent family‑visa threshold rises; exempt NHS and care staff from skills charges.
- Speed up asylum decisions (three‑month standard), allow work after three months, expand safe and legal routes; make Windrush compensation independent; simplify rules; end landlord status checks.

Rights and political reform
- Protect human rights law and international commitments; ban conversion practices; revise protest and surveillance laws; expand VAWG services; flexible working rights; disability employment support and accessibility; update gender recognition processes.
- Introduce proportional representation (STV), votes at 16, a cap on donations, a statutory Ministerial Code, Lords reform, stronger transparency and whistleblower protections, citizens’ assemblies, and wider devolution within a federal framework.

Defence and international
- Increase defence spending towards 2.5% of GDP; rebuild army numbers; retain nuclear deterrent with multilateral disarmament goals; tighter arms‑export controls; fix procurement; improve service housing and family support; deepen European and NATO cooperation.
- Support Ukraine (including using frozen Russian assets), restore aid to 0.7% with priorities on poverty, climate and education; rebuild European ties via agencies and mutual agreements with a long‑term aim of Single Market participation; pursue a ceasefire and two‑state solution in the Middle East; support Hong Kongers, Uyghurs and Taiwan.
